note:
The size this atlas has already reached, per measure. The build FAILS if any of these goes backwards.

Every bug this project has shipped to the public site was a silent SHRINKAGE, not a crash. build-surnames.py read the family archives through a path CI does not have, so the deployed dataset lost every archive attestation — Lerena lost Argentina and Uruguay, Defranceski lost Croatia — and eleven builds went green over the top of it. A gate that only asks «is the file there» cannot see that. A gate that asks «is it still as big as it was» can.

A floor is not a target. Raise one only when a real gain has been verified, with scripts/raise-floors.py, and never to make a failing build pass.

lowered.why: A DELIBERATE SHRINK, WHICH IS THE ONE THING THIS FILE EXISTS TO MAKE SOMEBODY EXPLAIN. A surname mentioned once in a family archive used to inherit that archive's entire country list — which is how «D'Arcy, attested in Cuba» reached the live site, from a single passing mention in the Defranceschi archive, whose own name appears 830 times. Names now need three mentions or more, unless the archive is small enough that its whole list is deliberate. 1,580 names stopped inheriting a geography they had no claim to; fewer names carry a non-register country; fewer qualify for phonetic clustering; the variant count falls. THE DATA GOT SMALLER BY GETTING MORE CORRECT, and the floor follows it down rather than the fix being abandoned to keep a number up.
